newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 8.04 pct to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 8.04 pct to new record close.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged in hectic activity spearheaded by bluechips on Monday amid rising hopes for a new, Islamist-free coalition to be set up by conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 1,774, up 132 points, or 8.04 percent from Friday and compared to a previous record close of 1,700 on January 27.
Trade volume soared to 45.48 trillion lira ($311 million) from Friday's 27.12 trillion ($185.9 million).
The index which gained 3.7 percent last week due to sharp rises prompted by fresh political optimism in the last two days, also exceeded the previous trading record of 1,751.
"The index had some difficulty in overcoming the 1,750 mark in the afternoon, but kept up the dynamism. Liquidity inflow was also quite good," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.

"The more the chance of a new government winning a vote of confidence rises, the better the market will be. There will be profit-taking, but as long as the political developments are positive, the short-term target will be 2,000 levels," he added.
Prime minister-designate anad Motherland Party (ANAP) leader Yilmaz said he saw no chance of failure in his bid to form a secularist coalition to keep the Islamists out of power.

He will on Tuesday meet leaders of four political parties -- conservative True Path (DYP) headed by caretaker Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, two leftist opposition parties and a small rightist party which broke away from the DYP.
Yilmaz who is around a dozen votes short of the simple majority needed to win a confidence vote said he would submit a cabinet list to President Suleyman Demirel on June 30.
He was nominated last week after the resignation of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan who quit after months of open criticism from the secularist army.
